candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: Using only U (free-stream velocity), nu (kinematic viscosity), x (streamwise distance) and y (wall-normal distance), dimensional analysis yields a single relevant dimensionless independent variable (the Blasius similarity variable) eta = y * sqrt(U/(nu x)). Therefore the streamwise velocity normalized by U is a dimensionless function of eta: u/U = f(eta). This is consistent because U has dimensions L T^-1, nu has L^2 T^-1, x and y have L, and the combination y*sqrt(U/(nu x)) is dimensionless.

variables.reason: The problem defines U as the free-stream velocity (magnitude of uniform velocity far from the plate). The KB record pq_free_stream_velocity is the canonical free-stream/edge velocity for boundary layers and explicitly uses symbol variants U∞, U_e and U; it defines velocity of the undisturbed flow outside a boundary layer, matching the role of U in the Blasius problem. That KB entry gives dimensions L T^-1, which supports the candidate SI exponents (L^1, T^-1) present in the ledger. All known coordinates (length and time exponents) are present and matched.

The ledger labels nu as kinematic viscosity. KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity is the canonical definition (ν = dynamic viscosity / density) and explicitly gives SI dimension L^2 T^-1, which matches the candidate exponents (L^2, T^-1). The KB entry applies directly because kinematic viscosity is a standard input in viscous boundary-layer problems like Blasius.

The ledger defines x as the streamwise distance measured along the plate from the leading edge. KB record pq_streamwise_distance is the canonical streamwise distance/coordinate used in boundary-layer contexts and lists SI dimension L, matching the candidate exponent (L^1). The KB entry is directly relevant because Blasius theory uses x as the coordinate along the plate from the leading edge.

The ledger defines y as the wall-normal distance from the plate. KB record pq_wall_normal_distance is the canonical wall-normal coordinate used in boundary-layer and wall-bounded flow definitions and lists SI dimension L, matching the candidate exponent (L^1). This entry applies because Blasius uses y as the coordinate normal to the wall.

final_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: Using only U (free-stream velocity), nu (kinematic viscosity), x (streamwise distance) and y (wall-normal distance), dimensional analysis yields a single relevant dimensionless independent variable (the Blasius similarity variable) eta = y * sqrt(U/(nu x)). Therefore the streamwise velocity normalized by U is a dimensionless function of eta: u/U = f(eta). This is consistent because U has dimensions L T^-1, nu has L^2 T^-1, x and y have L, and the combination y*sqrt(U/(nu x)) is dimensionless.
